title: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Transfer of Pioneer awards
sections.summary: Clause 4 adds a new Part IV to the Act for transferring Pioneer Industry, Pioneer Service and Development and Expansion awards between companies, and extends the Investment Allowance scheme to corporate partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of this Bill introduces a new Part IV to the Act for the transfer of the Pioneer Industry award, Pioneer Service award and Development and Expansion award between companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The second change extends the Investment Allowance scheme, or IA for short, to corporate partnerships.

sections.label: Investment Allowance for submarine cables
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced in Budget 2018 that the Investment Allowance for productive equipment would be extended to capital expenditure on newly-constructed submarine cable systems landing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Lastly, to encourage companies to invest in submarine cable systems landing in Singapore, the Minister for Finance announced in Budget 2018 that the IA for productive equipment would be extended to include capital expenditure incurred on newly-constructed submarine cable systems landing in Singapore approved by the Minister.

sections.label: Funds to protect against sea levels
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong announced at the National Day Rally that Singapore would probably need $100 billion to protect against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in his National Day Rally last year announced we would probably need $100 billion to protect ourselves against rising sea levels.

sections.label: Stranded fossil fuel assets estimate
sections.summary: A 2018 study estimated that globally, US$12 trillion of fossil fuel assets might be stranded by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A study published in 2018 estimated that globally, US$12 trillion of fossil fuel assets might be stranded by 2035.

sections.label: Low-carbon jobs estimate
sections.summary: A 2018 report by the Global Commission on the Economy and Climate estimated over 65 million new low-carbon jobs could be generated globally in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2018 report by the Global Commission on the Economy and Climate estimated that over 65 million new low-carbon jobs could be generated globally in 2030.

sections.label: Alternative meat market and EEIA
sections.summary: The alternative meat market is expected to grow to US$470 billion by 2040, and the speaker urged aligning tax incentives with a carbon-neutral economy and asked whether EEIA tax relief criteria could consider greenhouse gas emission reduction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The alternative meat market is expected to grow to US$470 billion by 2040, equivalent to a 17 times expansion in the next 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am proud to see local start-up Shiok Meats entering the arena.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to align our tax incentives with a carbon-neutral economy, so that we can attract and grow more of such champions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share whether the qualifying criteria for tax relief under the EEIA can include consideration for the potential of the activity to reduce greenhouse gas emissions either directly or indirectly?

sections.label: Short answer to questions
sections.summary: The short answer to both questions is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The short answer to both questions is yes.

sections.label: Incentive applications priority criteria
sections.summary: Applications for incentives, including under the EEIA, will prioritise investments aligned to national objectives, with carbon emissions an important but not sole criterion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: When assessing applications for incentives, including those under the EEIA, we will give priority to investments that are aligned to our national objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Carbon emissions is an important consideration, but it is not the only criterion.
